name: Back forward cache
plain: The browser freezes a left page whole and restores it instantly on Back, with scripts and state intact.
meaning: A person who leaves and presses Back can resume the same JavaScript heap, form values and open connections. Analytics must treat pageshow with persisted=true as a new view. The page can run no code while frozen.

access.persistence: Chrome keeps pages about 10 minutes (up to 6 entries on Android is not documented, verify)
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can freeze this page when you leave and bring it back instantly on Back
limits.user_action: You tap Back or Forward to return to the page.
can: Keep the page exactly how you left it
Restore your scroll spot and typed text
Run a bit of code when the page comes back
cannot: Keep the page running while it is frozen
Keep it frozen for long, since browsers drop it after a few minutes or when memory is low
Freeze pages that hold certain open connections

story.what_it_is: The browser freezes a page you leave and restores it instantly when you press Back.

marketing.name: Back/forward cache
marketing.pitch: Google pitches it as a way to make Back and Forward feel instant by keeping whole pages in memory.

story.for_you: You press Back and the page returns in an instant, exactly as you left it, scroll spot and typed text included. You did not wait for it to load.
story.for_makers: Makers love it because a fast Back button keeps people browsing and buying. They must make sure the page restores safely, for example by refreshing timers and logins after the restore.

use_cases.example: You open a product, press Back, and the search results return instantly with your scroll spot saved.
You read a story, press Back, and the front page comes back with nothing reloaded.
A browser game page is frozen when you leave and resumes at once, unless it blocks the freeze with open connections.
An ad script has to handle a page restored from the cache, or it counts one view and misses the next.
A measurement tool uses the restore event to count a Back visit as a new page view.
A bank page asks the browser not to freeze it, so a returning user must log in again.
A feed page returns instantly after you view a photo and keeps your place.

technical_bounds: Pages with unload handlers or open WebSockets may be excluded
Cache-Control: no-store pages are mostly excluded
Cannot run timers or fetches while frozen

abuse: Stale data after restore, double counted analytics

history.change: Cache-Control: no-store pages begin to be eligible in a gradual rollout (verify)
